previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a patient with alcoholic and hepatitis C-related cirrhosis and a history of hepatocellular carcinoma, was admitted with left lower quadrant abdominal pain, profuse watery diarrhea, nausea, and vomiting. His symptoms were similar to a prior C. difficile infection. CT imaging showed no acute abdominal process, colitis, or obstruction, with findings consistent with stable post-cholecystectomy changes and cirrhosis. He was started empirically on oral metronidazole for suspected recurrent C. difficile colitis. His symptoms improved, he tolerated a diet, and stool testing confirmed C. difficile. He remained stable with no liver decompensation, continued on home medications, and was discharged home on a full 14-day course of metronidazole with instructions for a bland diet and follow-up.
problems: Other and unspecified noninfectious gastroenteritis and colitis

Chronic hepatitis C without mention of hepatic coma
Malignant neoplasm of liver, not specified as primary or secondary

Brief Hospital Course:
# Diarrhea/abdominal pain:  This was likely secondary to known 
C.diff colitis.  Patient had similar presentation to ___ in 
___ and was treated with flagyl for 14 days with resolution 
of his symptoms.  He seems to have responded to PO vancomycin at 
this time and will require a prolonged course given the recent 
recurrence.  He had no evidence of ascites on exam and 
ultrasound performed on admission did not reveal any abdominal 
fluid.  UA and culture negative.  He remains guaiac negative and 
Hct is near baseline.  The patient was afebrile with a normal 
WBC.  He was tolerating a regular diet with no pain by 
discharge.  He will complete a 7 week taper of PO vancomycin and 
will start Saccharomyces boulardii 500 mg orally twice daily 
while on antibiotics.  He should continue the probiotic for two 
weeks after antibiotic course is complete (9 total weeks of 
therapy).  The vancomycin taper was explained to the patient in 
detail with an interpretor and he is understanding of how to 
take these two medications over the next 2 months.  He will 
follow-up with his PCP, ID physician and ___ shortly 
after discharge
  
# Hyponatremia: Admission sodium was 130 which improved with IV 
fluids.  This is likely hypovolemic hyponatremia in setting of 
vomiting and diarrhea.  Patient also received albumin on night 
of admission.  Home lasix and spironolactone were held during 
admission as the patient had diarrhea but were resumed on 
discharge as diarrhea improved and patient was tolerating PO 
diet.    
  
# Hep C cirrhosis: Gastritis seen on EGD in ___ but no 
evidence of varices. No history of HE or SBP. ALT and AP are 
elevated though are similar to prior values.   As mentioned, we 
held lasix and spironolactone for now given hypovolemia and 
hyponatremia but they were resumed on discharge as diarrhea 
improved and patient was tolerating PO diet.  He was continued 
on home omeprazole and nadolol while in the hospital. 
  
# HCC: S/p RFA and chemoembolization. AFP on ___ was within 
normal limits.  
  
# CODE: Full (confirmed)

Discharge Instructions:
You were admitted to the hospital with abdominal discomfort and 
diarrhea.  You were found to have a C.diff colitis at an outside 
hospital and were started on the appropriate antibiotics.  While 
here, you were treated with oral vancomycin with improvement in 
your symptoms.  You will need a long course of this medication.  
You tolerated a regular diet and your diarrhea improved by 
discharge.  You are being discharged home with plans to 
follow-up with your primary care physician, liver doctor and 
infectious disease doctor. 

The following changes were made to your medications:
1.  START vancomycin 125mg by mouth for 7 weeks.  Take the 
medication as follows
    a.  125 mg orally four times daily for 14 days 
    b.  125 mg orally twice daily for 7 days 
    c.  125 mg orally once daily for 7 days 
    d.  125 mg orally every other day for 7 days 
    e.  125 mg orally every 3 days for 14 days 

2.  START Saccharomyces boulardii 500 mg orally twice daily for 
9 weeks
3.  STOP taking your docusate until you recover from this 
infection and your diarrhea has resolved.

No other changes were made to your medications
